claim: The closing diff is not instruction-neutral on the all-literal workload. Moving `literal_twin` into `node.rs` (F3) adds about 6.2M Ir to extraction relative to r3, with no semantic change. fixes.md calls the regression "found and fixed", but it was only reduced.
evidence: Callgrind is deterministic, and the profiles show this. r3 (8da7c86): `extract_dag_over` inclusive 1,136,559,328 and total 6,305,898,607. c1/close1: 1,142,798,209 and 6,311,544,165. That is +6,238,881 Ir (+0.55%) in extraction and +5.65M in total (+0.247% vs base, where r3 was +0.158%). Saturation went down 278K. Diffing cg-annotate.a3-r3.txt against cg-annotate.a3-close1.txt puts the increase in SharedPricer `Settlement::relax` (+3.25M), TreePricer `relax` (+1.23M), `Selection::price` (+0.54M) and `BinaryHeap::pop` (+0.88M). The only extraction-side source change is the `literal_twin` call at those three price sites, and `pop` was not touched at all. That pattern points to codegen-unit and inlining placement, not new algorithmic work. Semantics are untouched: byteprobe (both tiers), gate1b (29 font programs' nodes, keys and digests), gate2 and gate2x are IDENTICAL to base, and gate2.jsonl differs only in `wall_clock_us`. Wall time is not usable evidence either way. r1 to r3 have equal Ir (6,305,896,638 and 6,305,898,607) but medians 1014 then 1116 ms, and close1-b and c1 differ by 87 ms on equal Ir. I re-ran the head bin.measure on an idle host (load 0.09) and got 1011-1274 ms. The +20.9% wall figure vs base is therefore uncontrolled. The measure still passes the +0.5% total limit.
fix: Either record it truthfully in fixes.md ("the closing pass costs +5.6M Ir on the literal path, from code placement of the moved `literal_twin`"), or keep the fast path at the call site and re-measure. For the second option: an `#[inline(always)]` guard that returns `None` unless the node is a `Reduce` with `arity() > 1`, calling a non-inlined body that does the `discover`/`reduce` work.

claim: The new paragraph on `EGraph::admit_unit` names the wrong caller. It says "Its caller holds the unit's body" and calls `runtime::Program::of` the only caller outside tests. The only non-test caller is `runtime::saturate`, and it holds only `job.leaves` (key to variance), not any body.
evidence: `grep admit_unit` finds one non-test call: pixelflow-search/src/runtime.rs:733-734, `for (&key, &variance) in job.leaves { egraph.admit_unit(key, variance); }` inside `fn saturate`. `Program::of` (runtime.rs:276-321) builds the `Unit`s, and `Program::optimize` (:336) turns them into the leaves map. The substance holds: every leaf comes through `Program::of`'s `free_index` check. I also confirmed that the new refusal cannot fire on a production unit. A `Ref` comes only from `ExprArena::push_ref`, whose only minting caller is `Kernel::by_ref` (kernel.rs:1069); the other callers copy an existing `Ref`. `by_ref` asserts `free_index(root).is_none()` first (kernel.rs:1058). No non-test code in pixelflow-graphics, core-term, pixelflow-runtime or pixelflow-core calls `by_ref`, `push_ref` or `KernelStore::intern`; every hit is under tests/ or `mod tests`. So a font program holds no `Ref`, `holds_a_ref` is false, `Program::of` returns at :277 before the unit loop, and the new check is never reached. gate1b and gate2 are identical.
fix: Reword along these lines: "This sees a variance and nothing else... The runtime tier's unit walk (`runtime::Program::of`) holds each unit's body and refuses an open one by `ExprArena::free_index`; every variance `runtime::saturate`, the only caller outside tests, admits is one that walk produced."

claim: `of_var`'s new paragraph says "no check of closedness or placement may read a variance". Codegen placement does read a variance, and the same sentence then cites codegen as the compliant case. The doc contradicts the code it points to.
evidence: pixelflow-codegen/src/program/lower.rs:150 `let variance = compute_arena_variance(arena);`. This feeds `lane_uniform`, and the function doc says "Every def carries the variance of the node it was lowered from, which scoping places it by". lower.rs's own new doc is accurate: "The variance this reads types a placeholder as constant, so this is the refusal that stops one from being placed."
fix: Say what holds. Closedness is never judged by a variance. Placement reads one only on a term from which a `Var` that is no fold's binder has already been refused (codegen's `Var` arm). Both ask `ExprArena::free_index`, or refuse such a `Var`, before they trust a variance.

claim: The panic now also names an escaped fold index, but its ending ("this schedule was built without the lowering pipeline") is false for that case. A top-level open kernel goes through the whole pipeline and reaches this arm. `Binder::from_var`'s doc, which this refusal now depends on, does not say that a placeholder maps to `None`.
evidence: This is from reading the code; I did not build an end-to-end repro. The only `free_index` callers are `Kernel::by_ref`, `ExprArena::admit` and `Program::of`, and `Program::of` checks units only, returning early when the term holds no `Ref` (runtime.rs:277). `passes::lattice::collapse` ignores a placeholder: lattice.rs:179-182 only marks slots `Binder::from_var` accepts. `pipeline::compile` refuses retired axes by name (pipeline.rs:127-132) but not placeholders. So a kernel built from an escaped index (e.g. `Lattice::bake` of the leaked `i`) panics here with a cause it does not have. pixelflow-ir/src/fold.rs:210 documents `from_var` as "`None` if that index is a lattice coordinate or a retired axis". The new test `a_surviving_placeholder_fails_loudly` relies on `None` for a placeholder as well.
fix: Split the message by case: a coordinate means collapse was skipped; an index at or past the binder slots is an open kernel. pipeline.rs already states that boundary's own reasoning for retired axes, so `pipeline::compile` could refuse `free_index(root)` by name instead. Add placeholders to `Binder::from_var`'s `None` list.

claim: `literal_twin`'s doc says "Because they are one function the two cannot disagree about which folds have a literal form or what it is". `KnownBound`'s doc (fold_rules.rs:541-543) says the rule's form and the priced form "are the same". Both over-claim, and both restate the agreement that F3 asked the docs to stop asserting.
evidence: The two callers pass different `literal` oracles. `KnownBound::apply` uses `egraph.nodes(class).find_map(ENode::literal)`, the first literal member. The price sites use the literal of the form the DP chose for the class (`self.chosen[...]`, or `self.node(egraph, pick_of(class)).literal()`). Whether a fold has a literal form therefore depends on which oracle is asked. One function guarantees only that the same literals give the same fold.
fix: Say what one function buys: "given the same literal for each bound class, the rule and the price build the same fold, because there is one construction; which literal each finds is its own (a class member for the rule, the chosen form for the price)". Make the same change to `KnownBound`'s sentence.

claim: Several texts still describe the walk as it was before sites (F2): `representative`'s doc, `substitute`'s summary, the plan's L7 sentence, and the "no builder makes one" justification.
evidence: `representative` (:394-396) says "The node a substitution rebuilds `class` through: its first", but it is now only the `Site::Body` choice. `substitute`'s summary (:193) says "walking one member per e-class", but a class is walked once per (class, site) (`Memo.body`/`Memo.bound`). The plan's L7 (docs/language/2026-10-20-a-bound-is-a-value.md:200) says "A class reached as a bound is rebuilt through its first member that keeps L3", while the code, and the module doc's "under a nested fold's value bound", apply the rule to every class under a bound. :224-225 and `of_child` (:352) say a fold inside a value bound is something "no builder makes". The graph can still put a `Reduce` member into a bound's class by union (a fold over one trip that peels and empties to its body, merged with that body's class). `Site::member` also returns the first lawful member even when it is a `Reduce`, so such a class declines although a later lawful non-fold member exists. That costs completeness only.
fix: Have `representative`'s doc say "under a body" and the summary say "one member per e-class and site". Change L7 to "a class reached as a bound, or under one". Replace "which no builder makes" with what is true ("which the walk does not enter: its body would need the law lifted by its own binder"), or have `member` skip a `Reduce` under a bound.

claim: Small dead-code and convention issues in the F2 code. `Site` derives comparisons nothing uses. `Site::member` passes a fixed `BoundEnd::Hi` for both ends, which holds only by a comment's convention. One test assertion can never fail.
evidence: `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] enum Site`: no `==`, ordering or map key on `Site` exists. `Memo` keys on `(EClassId, Fold)` and every use is a `match`. `fold.admits_bound(BoundEnd::Hi, reads).is_ok()` (:347) is right only because `admits_bound`'s result ignores `end` (fold.rs:693-699). The `Site` doc carries that convention ("the end only names a refusal"), and CLAUDE.md says a convention held in a comment will eventually be broken. In `a_nested_bound_is_rebuilt_through_the_member_that_keeps_l3`, the loop after `run` (:2064-2079) checks every value bound's class fact against COORDS ∪ binder(0). `EGraph::add`'s `refuse_a_varying_bound` already enforces exactly that for every fold added, and a class fact only shrinks under union. The loop cannot fail; the test's real assertion is that nothing panics.
fix: Derive only `Clone, Copy`. Give `Fold` an end-free predicate (for example `fn bound_may_read(self, reads: Variance) -> bool`) that `admits_bound` and `Site::member` both call, so no fabricated `BoundEnd` is passed. Drop the vacuous loop, or replace it with an assertion that can fail: for example, that the inner folds' value bounds in the graph read `i + k` spellings and no `Sub`.

claim: F2 is incomplete. `PlanBuilder::substitute` picks a bound's member by that member's variance over its children's current class facts. But the bound node it rebuilds can hash-cons into a class that already exists, and that class's `var_fact` can be stale: it is seeded at birth and "never repaired upward" (graph/columns.rs:299). `EGraph::add`'s backstop reads exactly that class fact (`refuse_a_varying_bound`, graph.rs:435), so saturation still panics with `BoundVaries` on a bound the rule built through a lawful member. This happens even when the bound is the bare outer index, where the member is `Var(i)` itself and HalveFold's leaf builds `i + s`. Three docs are therefore false: `substitute`'s "the member's variance judged before the substitution is the law's answer after it" (:214-219), HalveFold's "`EGraph::add` accepts it because the rule builds it only through a member … that already keeps L3" (:443), and the plan's L7 sentence (docs/language/2026-10-20-a-bound-is-a-value.md:200).
evidence:
Scratch crate /home/user/scratch/a3-close-review (src/main.rs; outputs in probe-results.txt). The backtrace in every panicking case is: refuse_a_varying_bound <- EGraph::add <- NodeSink::make <- plan_shape <- apply_action <- commit <- sweep_rule <- saturate.

(1) stale_halve2, HalveFold alone, n=4 (the shape of the ruling's minimal pin):
- Build x=Var(0), i=Var(slot1), K=(i+X)-X, P=K+1, Q=((i+X)+1)-X.
- union(K,i), rebuild. union(P,Q), rebuild. This re-keys P's node as `i+1`, and P's fact stays {X,i}.
- Add the nested Σ_{j<i} X·j. Its bound class is i, fact {i}, so it is admitted.
- Add the outer Σ_{i<4}. compatibility(1) then panics: "BoundVaries: a fold's hi bound varies with Variance{X,i5}".

(2) stale_peel, PeelFold alone, n=1:
- P=(X-X)+1, then union(X-X, 0). The nested bound is i+1.
- The peel rebuilds the bound as 0+1, which hash-conses into P (fact {X}), and the run panics with BoundVaries, Variance{X}.

(3) stale_halve3 under all_rules()++fold_rules(), which is RuleSet::runtime(), with compatibility(12):
- As (2) for halve, plus `1+K` unioned into P before K=i, so neither `i+1` nor `1+i` is born fresh afterwards.
- Panics at n=2, 4 and 8.
- Without the commuted spelling (stale_halve2 under the full set), commutativity births a fresh lawful `1+i` and repairs P. Under the full set, constant folding repairs the peel case.

Every union above is an equation the algebra derives: commutativity, (a+b)-b=a, reassociation, x-x=0. This is the same hand-made-union standard as the ruling's own pins.

I found no arena-only trigger. I ran 616 arena kernels under RuleSet::runtime() with compatibility(12), covering spellings of i through X, Y and j, constants c in {1,2,4}, junk in the outer or nested body, bound i or i+1, and n in {1,2,3,4,8,16}. None panicked (sweep-release.txt, gen-*.txt).
fix:
Make the decline see the class a rebuilt bound lands in, not only the member's own variance. Two ways:
- In `plan_shape`'s HeadNode::Reduce arm, check each value bound after it is resolved with `Fold::admits_bound` against its class fact, and abandon the action (no union) instead of calling `add`.
- Or resolve the bound's nodes in the planner (a pub(crate) memo lookup) and return None when a lookup hits a class whose fact fails L3.
Either way, literal folds (arity 1) are never looked at, so today's kernels stay byte-identical. Refining a class's fact on every memo hit is also sound under the var_fact law, but it touches literal kernels too. Then correct the three docs, and pin stale_halve3 under RuleSet::runtime() plus the two single-rule cases as should-not-panic tests.

claim: Pre-existing at base, not introduced by A3. Bearing on F1: an escaped fold index is silently captured by the next fold whose `BinderScope` reclaims the same placeholder bit. After capture, `free_index` (the closedness check F1 relies on) reports the term closed, `by_ref` accepts it, and the program reads the wrong binder. Separately, `Kernel::over`'s doc still says "an index cannot escape the fold that binds it". That is false, and it contradicts the new `Variance::of_var` doc and the F1 pin, which is itself an escape. No variance-based check passes a placeholder silently: Program::of, arena_to_schedule's Var arm, by_ref/admit and lower_dwrt all hold.
evidence:
The `capture` mode of /home/user/scratch/a3-close-review:
- `let l` escapes from `Kernel::sum_over(2, |i| { leaked = Some(i.clone()); i.clone() })` as Var(64), with free_index Some(64).
- `Kernel::sum_over(3, |k| k.mul(&Kernel::constant(10.0)).add(&l))` gives `reduce[add_4[0..3)](add(mul(Var(4), Const(10)), Var(4)))` with free_index None. That is Σ_k 11k, not Σ_k (10k + l).
- `.by_ref()` returns Ref(0xd678089b841cca4e).

The same output comes at base: /home/user/scratch/a3-close-review-base, built against /home/user/scratch/a3-r2/base-src, whose kernel.rs and arena.rs are identical to 3bfdaded.
fix: Correct the doc now: an index can escape through a clone, and a later fold that reclaims its placeholder captures it, which no check sees. Track the capture itself as a known hole (it needs placeholders that are never reissued, or an index identity outside Var(u8)). It is not A3's to close.

claim: The GrowthPredictor doc is now stale. It says `pending` "is only probed, inserted into and counted, never iterated, so the capacity it keeps between predictions is not observable", but the closing diff's `GrowthPredictor::fact` iterates `pending` with a linear `find_map` to find the node a pending id names.
evidence: graph.rs:1426-1436: `self.pending.iter().find_map(|(node, &id)| (id == class).then_some(node))`, called recursively for each pending child. The answer does not depend on order because ids are unique. The cost does: a hashbrown scan is proportional to bucket count, and `predict` clears `pending` but keeps its capacity (graph.rs:1119). So the capacity is now observable as cost, which the doc denies. This runs only on value-bound folds and does not touch the literal path.
fix: Either keep the doc's promise and give `fact` an id-to-node lookup (pending ids are minted sequentially from `num_classes()`), or amend the doc: the table is iterated only by `fact`, whose answer is order-independent because ids are unique; its cost scales with the retained capacity and is paid only for a fold's value bound.

claim: The new paragraph in `EGraph::admit_unit`'s doc names the wrong caller. It says "Its caller holds the unit's body … (`runtime::Program::of`, the only caller outside tests)". The only caller outside tests is `runtime::saturate`, which holds no body, only `job.leaves` (key to variance).
evidence: `grep admit_unit` finds one non-test call, runtime.rs:734 in `fn saturate`: `for (&key, &variance) in job.leaves { egraph.admit_unit(key, variance); }`. `Program::of` (runtime.rs:280-322) is where each body is resolved and refused by `free_index` (runtime.rs:307). It builds the leaves map later in `Program::optimize` (runtime.rs:336) and never calls `admit_unit`.
fix: Reword: "Its only caller outside tests, `runtime::saturate`, admits the leaves `runtime::Program::of` built, and `Program::of` refused an open unit by `ExprArena::free_index` when it resolved the body: closedness is judged there, on the term."

claim: The new `of_var` paragraph overstates the rule. "So no check of closedness or placement may read a variance" is false of the code it cites. `Program::of` reads a variance as one of its two closedness checks, and codegen placement is driven by `compute_arena_variance`.
evidence: runtime.rs:268-274 says "Two checks … The variance assertion judges what the unit varies with; `free_index` judges what it leaves unbound", and runtime.rs:299-306 asserts on the unit's variance. pixelflow-codegen/src/program/lower.rs:150 computes `compute_arena_variance(arena)` to place every def, and the `Var` arm (lower.rs:192) is the refusal that keeps a placeholder out. The intended meaning is that closedness is never concluded from a variance alone.
fix: Say what it means: "So a variance never decides closedness: a closedness check asks `ExprArena::free_index`, which counts a placeholder free (`Kernel::by_ref`, the runtime tier's unit walk), and placement, which does read a variance, refuses a `Var` that is no fold's binder (codegen's lowering)."

claim: `substitute`'s doc explains the graph-side decline only as a rebuilt bound that "resolve[s] to a class that already exists, seeded wider than the term". A freshly minted bound class can also be seeded wider than its term, by inheriting the fact of a child that landed in a stale class. The behavior is right; the doc and `plan_shape`'s matching sentence describe a narrower case than the one the check covers.
evidence: `add` seeds a new class with `node.variance(.., |child| var_fact[root(child)])` (graph.rs, the `add` body), so an op's fact is the union of its children's facts. Example: nested bound `(i + 1)·2` under `PeelFold` (i := 0), with `P = (X − X) + 1` stale as in `stale_zero_plus_one`. Then `0 + 1` lands in P (fact {X}), `P·2` is minted fresh with fact {X}, and `refuses` reads that fact and declines. So "a node this plan mints is as lawful as the member it was read from" holds only for the term, not for the fact `add` reads. graph.rs:1771 ("hash-consing can resolve a lawful term to a class seeded wider than it") has the same gap. No test pins the inherited case.
fix: State the covered condition: the graph declines any plan fold whose bound's class fact fails L3, whether the bound landed in a stale class or was minted over a child that did. Optionally pin the `(i + 1)·2` case beside `stale_zero_plus_one`.

claim: Dead code left over from an earlier design. `Site` derives `PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord`, and nothing uses them: the memo keys on `(EClassId, Fold)`, not `Site`. Also, `representative` now has a single caller (`Site::member`'s `Body` arm), and its doc "The node a substitution rebuilds `class` through: its first" is no longer true under a bound.
evidence: `grep Site` in fold_rules.rs shows only constructions and `match`es, no comparison or ordering. The `Memo` maps are `BTreeMap<EClassId, Done>` and `BTreeMap<(EClassId, Fold), Done>` (fold_rules.rs:383-386). `representative` is called only at fold_rules.rs:349, and its doc is at :405-406.
fix: Drop the unused derives (keep `Clone, Copy`). Either inline `egraph.nodes(class).next()` into the `Body` arm and delete `representative`, or restate its doc as "under a body".

claim: `Site::member`'s `Bound` arm can return a fold member, and then `of_child` declines the whole rewrite even when a later member of the same class keeps L3. The doc justifies the decline with "(which no builder makes)" (:235, :363). Saturation, not a builder, can put a fold into a bound's class, for example `PeelFold` unioning `Σ_{k<1} i` with `i`.
evidence: `Site::member` is `egraph.nodes(class).find(|node| fold.admits_bound(..).is_ok())`, with no exclusion of `ENode::Reduce`. `of_child` returns `None` for any child of a `Reduce` under `Site::Bound`, and `substitute` propagates that with `?` (fold_rules.rs:290). This costs completeness only, never soundness, and is unreachable on literal kernels.
fix: In the `Bound` arm, skip `ENode::Reduce` members (`!matches!(node, ENode::Reduce { .. }) && admits_bound(..)`). Then a fold under a bound is never chosen, and the "no builder makes one" justification is no longer needed.

claim: Two of the new F2 tests assert less than their docs say. In `a_rebuilt_bound_that_lands_in_a_stale_class_is_declined`, `assert!(eg.num_classes() >= classes, "classes only grow")` cannot fail, because an e-graph never removes a class. `the_runtime_rules_saturate_a_graph_with_a_stale_bound_class` says "the bound lands in `P` at every level … and the graph declines it each time", but asserts neither a landing nor a decline.
evidence: fold_rules.rs:2455-2459 is the vacuous assertion. In the runtime-set test (the one after it), the assertions are only `every_bound_keeps_l3`, an extracted bound reading only the outer index, and `free_index == None`. If a later rule repaired P (the doc itself notes commutativity can mint a lawful twin), the test would pass without ever reaching `refuses`. The round's notes record that both tests fail with the check removed, which holds today but is not pinned.
fix: Replace the vacuous assertion with what the doc promises: for example, that the pre-refusal nodes stayed and the prediction counted them, or simply delete it. In the runtime-set test, also assert after saturation that `P`'s fact still reads X and that some plan was declined (for example, that the value-bounded inner fold count is below the control's).

claim: Small inaccuracy in `literal_twin`'s doc: "a fold over literals, a leaf and an operation answer on the first test". A fold over literals passes the first test (`let ENode::Reduce { header, .. } = self else`) and returns on the second (`header.arity() == 1`).
evidence: node.rs:442-447: first the `Reduce` pattern, which returns for leaves and ops; then `if header.arity() == 1 { return None; }`, which returns for literal folds.
fix: "a leaf and an operation answer on the first test, a fold over literals on the second."

claim: No defect: every lens check on the literal path passes. (1) Gates are identical to base on the final tree. (2) `Program::of`'s new `free_index` refusal never fires on a production unit, because the 29 font programs have no units. (3) The F2 member walk and the graph's refusal read only a fold's header unless the fold has a value bound. (4) The closing pass adds no algorithmic work on literal folds; its Ir moves are within this binary's layout noise and inside the gate limit.
evidence: Gates: `cmp` against base gives identical byteprobe avx2 and avx512, gate1b, gate2 and gate2x (*.a3-close2), and no tracked file outside .wip differs between d4bcd11 and HEAD. Production units: no production code mints a `Ref` except `Kernel::by_ref`; grep finds `.by_ref()` and `push_ref` only in pixelflow-ir internals that copy existing refs, and in tests. So `holds_a_ref` is false and `Program::of` returns before the loop. Any `Ref` that did exist would be minted by `by_ref`, which asserts `free_index(root).is_none()` on the same `parts()` the store returns (kernel.rs:1058-1066); linking Dwrt-reached refs inlines closed referents, which stay closed. In cg.a3-close2.out, `free_index` is called only from `ExprArena::admit` (1,028x), never from the unit walk, and the `BTreeMap<KernelKey, Unit>` drops total about 1.4K Ir (empty maps). Literal folds: a `Site::Bound` arises only at a `Reduce` child position > 0 (`of_child`), which exists only when `header.arity() > 1`. The body memo keys on the class alone, as before. `refuses` returns on `has_a_value_bound` before any canonicalization or fact read, in both sinks. `KnownBound` and the price sites call the same `literal_twin` body, which returns on the header. Measures: measure.a3-c2 vs base gives total Ir +0.193% (limit +0.5), saturate −0.131%, extraction +1.274% (A3's earlier rounds; r3 was +1.157%). The closing pass from r3 to close2 adds +2.23M Ir (+0.035%). Of that, +1.31M is in extraction, where extract.rs's only change is the `literal_twin` move. Extraction Ir swung by 4.9M between close1 and close2 with no extract.rs change, so this is inlining or layout. The other +0.39M is in saturate, from the walk's `Site` tag and the header test at each plan fold.
fix: None needed.

claim: The L7 sentence added in closing round 2 says a declined rewrite builds "no fold and making no union". The first half is false. `plan_shape` refuses a fold only when it reaches it, and every node made before that point stays in the graph, including a lawful nested fold earlier in the same plan. The code docs already say this: `plan_shape` (graph.rs, "The nodes built before the refusal stay") and `RewriteAction::Plan` (rewrite.rs).
evidence: Scratch probe in /home/user/scratch/a3-close3-review, `cargo build`, then `./target/debug/a3-close3-review orphan`. It sets up `P = (X − X) + 1`, joins `X − X` to `0`, and rebuilds. It then builds `Σ_{i<1}(Σ_{j<i} X·j + Σ_{j<i+1} X·j)` and runs `PeelFold` alone. The first nested bound peels to `0`, which is lawful, so the fold is made. The second peels to `0 + 1`, which lands in the stale class `P`; `refuses` fires there and the plan is declined. Output: `value-bounded inner folds 2 -> 3, classes 13 -> 14, outer members 1 -> 1`. The new class 13 is `Σ_{j < Value(class 3)} X·j`, an orphan fold, and the matched class gains no member. So no union was made, but a fold was built. With `--features tel` (`enable_growth_telemetry`, so `apply_measured` asserts the prediction exactly) the run also passes: the predictor counts the orphan correctly. The defect is only in the prose.
fix: Reword to: "...and the rewrite declines there too: it makes no union, and the nodes it made before that fold stay, as orphans that cost classes and never soundness (a lawful nested fold can be among them)". Optionally make `.wip/a3/spec.md` J27's "(its nodes before the `Reduce`)" say the same.

claim: J24 states the extraction-side hole too narrowly. It says the hole is reached "where a class holds no lawful member at all". In fact extraction materializes a coordinate-reading member whenever that member is the cheapest in a bound class, even when a dearer lawful member is present.
